title: Enzymatic measurements for the detection of trypsin and carboxypeptidase A inhibitory activity
protocol: Incubate in a quartz cell 10 μl of biological sample with 50 μl trypsin (33 μg ml^-1 in 20 mM CaCl2, 0.1 M Tris, pH 8.0) and 790 μl activity buffer (20 mM CaCl2, 0.1 M Tris, pH 8.0) for 3 min at room temperature.
Repeat Step 1 in another quartz cell and add 10 μl activity buffer instead of biological sample to obtain the control sample.
Add 150 μl of the substrate N-benzoyl-arginine ethyl ester hydrochloride to each quartz cell.
Gently mix all the quartz cells and measure the absorbance change at 254 nm and 25 °C over 2 min, producing 240 time points (signal averaging time = 0.5 s).

Incubate in a quartz cell 10 μl biological sample (from each re-dissolved chromatographic fraction) with 2 μl carboxypeptidase A (35 μg ml^-1 in 20 mM Tri-HCl buffer, 0.5 M NaCl, pH 7.5) and 978 μl activity buffer (20 mM Tri-HCl buffer, 0.5 M NaCl, pH 7.5) for 3 min at room temperature.
Repeat Step 1 in another quartz cell.
Add 10 μl of activity buffer to the quartz cell.
Add 10 μl of the substrate N-(4-methoxyphenylazoformyl)-Phe-OH to each quartz cell.
Measure absorbance change at 350 nm and 25°C over 3 min, producing 360 time points with a signal averaging time of 0.5 s.
Biological samples yielding slopes below 0.060 U.Abs. per min are taken for 'intensity fading MS' assays.
